title: Evaluation of a serialized literal
statement: Let $\ell=(v,b)$ be a literal, let $r,u,x,\mathrm{pre}$ be binary words, and let $c$ be a Boolean value. Suppose $v<|u|$ and $x$ is the concatenation of $\mathrm{pre}$ with the pair encoding of the literal encoding of $\ell$ followed by $r$, together with $u$. Starting with $|\mathrm{pre}|$ input bits consumed, in the clause-level evaluation state with accumulator $c$, work word $u$, and work head at $0$, the verifier is after exactly $3v+7$ steps in the clause-level evaluation state with accumulator $c\wedge[\alpha_u(v)=b]$, with $|\mathrm{pre}|+2|\mathrm{enc}(\ell)|$ input bits consumed, work word $u$, work head at $0$, and empty output.
replaced:
Let $\ell = (v, b)$ be a literal and $u$ a word with $v < |u|$, and let the input be
$x = p \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{pair}(\sigma \mathbin{+\!\!+} r, u)$ where $\sigma$ is the
serialization of $\ell$. Started in the clause-level evaluation state with accumulator
$c$, $|p|$ bits consumed, work word $u$, and head $0$, the non-tautology verifier after
exactly $3v + 7$ steps is in the clause-level state with accumulator
$c \wedge (\alpha_u(v) = b)$, where $\alpha_u$ reads $v$ off the $v$-th bit of $u$, with
$|p| + 2|\sigma|$ bits consumed and head $0$.
